items.stem: A business buys equipment for cash. How does the accounting equation respond?

options.text: One asset (equipment) rises and another asset (cash) falls, so the equation still balances
options.rationale: Correct: swapping one asset for another leaves total assets, and the equation, unchanged.

options.text: Assets rise and liabilities rise by the same amount
options.rationale: No liability is involved in a cash purchase.

options.text: Equity falls with no change to assets
options.rationale: Equity is unaffected by swapping one asset for another.
The equation always balances under double entry.

items.explanation: Correct: swapping one asset for another leaves total assets, and the equation, unchanged.

items.stem: Under the accrual basis, when is revenue recognised?

options.text: When it is earned, regardless of when cash is received
options.rationale: Correct: accrual accounting recognises revenue when earned.
That is the cash basis, not accrual.

options.text: At the start of the financial year
options.rationale: Timing follows the earning of revenue, not the calendar start.
Deleting an invoice is not a recognition event.

items.explanation: Correct: accrual accounting recognises revenue when earned.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the financial statements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Net profit from the income statement increases retained earnings in equity
options.rationale: Correct: profit flows into retained earnings on the balance sheet.

options.text: The cash flow statement explains the change in the cash balance over the period
options.rationale: Correct: it reconciles opening and closing cash across three activity types.

options.text: A profitable company always has a positive cash balance
options.rationale: Profit and cash differ; a profitable firm can still be short of cash.

options.text: The balance sheet reports performance over a period
options.rationale: The balance sheet is a point-in-time snapshot, not a period measure.

items.explanation: Correct: profit flows into retained earnings on the balance sheet.; Correct: it reconciles opening and closing cash across three activity types.
